articles.title: Pleading Licensee Marking After VDPP v. Volkswagen
articles.content:
联邦巡回法院维持裁定，驳回了一项专利侵权诉讼，因为专利持有人——一家拥有十一项和解许可证的非实施实体——未能就专利标记法规的遵守提出足够的陈述。VDPP有限责任公司诉福斯汽车集团美国公司案（案号2024-2226，联邦巡回法院2026年8月19日判决）。由于该专利已过期，唯一可能的救济措施是追溯性赔偿损失。但未能充分主张构成性或实际通知，导致这些追溯性损失也被否决。

上诉法院还维持了20万美元的律师费奖励，并由于缺乏上诉管辖权，驳回了上诉中关于反对VDPP律师威廉·拉梅的制裁部分。此前关于该案有两篇文章，包括对2024年原始制裁令和2026年4月口头辩论的讨论。

在上诉中，VDPP主要要求有机会修改其诉状。法院拒绝了这一请求，最终认为任何修改都是徒劳的：“我们看不到VDPP有任何修改诉状的方式，以合理地主张其已尽合理努力确保其许可证持有人遵守35 U.S.C. § 287法规。”

根据《专利法》，专利侵权通常可获得最多六年的追溯性赔偿损失（35 U.S.C. § 286）。然而，法律规定了一个关键限制：制造或销售专利产品的专利持有人，或授权他人制造或销售的专利持有人，必须在产品上标明专利号码，才能追溯赔偿。35 U.S.C. § 287(a)。若未标记，赔偿损失仅从被控侵权者收到实际侵权通知之日起计算。

VDPP未实施任何行为，因此无需为自身产品标记，但其已将该专利许可给了十一名和解被告。其拟修改的诉状未说明任何许可证持有人是否要求标记（或实际标记）。根据北极猫公司诉邦巴迪尔休闲产品公司案（950 F.3d 860，联邦巡回法院2020年），专利持人的许可证持有人也必须遵守§ 287，专利持人必须尽合理努力确保他们这样做。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The Federal Circuit has affirmed dismissal of a patent infringement complaint because the patentee, a non-practicing entity holding eleven settlement licenses, failed to plead compliance with the patent marking statute. VDPP, LLC v. Volkswagen Group of America, Inc., No. 2024-2226 (Fed. Cir. Aug. 19, 2026).  Since the patent had expired, the only potential remedy was back damages. But the failure to sufficiently allege either constructive or actual notice meant that those back damages were also lost.

The appellate court additionally affirmed a $200k attorney fee award and dismissed, for want of appellate jurisdiction, the portion of the appeal contesting sanctions against VDPP's counsel William Ramey. There are two prior posts about this case, including discussion of the original 2024 sanctions order and the April 2026 oral argument.

In the appeal, VDPP primarily asked for the opportunity to amend its complaint.  The panel refused -- ultimately concluding that any amendment would be futile: "we see no way for VDPP to amend its complaint to plausibly allege it made reasonable efforts to ensure its licensees complied with 35 U.S.C. § 287."

Under the Patent Act, up to six years of back damages are generally available for patent infringement. 35 U.S.C. § 286. However, the statute provides a key limitation: a patentee who makes or sells patented articles, or who licenses others to make or sell them, must mark those articles with the patent number in order to reach back at all. 35 U.S.C. § 287(a). Without marking, damages run only from the date the accused infringer received actual notice of the infringement.

VDPP practiced nothing and so had nothing of its own to mark, but it had licensed the asserted patent to eleven settling defendants, and its proposed amended complaint said nothing about whether any of them required marking (or actually marked). Under Arctic Cat Inc. v. Bombardier Recreational Products Inc., 950 F.3d 860 (Fed. Cir. 2020), a patentee's licensees must comply with § 287 too, and the patentee must make reasonable efforts to see that they do.
